newsitem.title: USA: PEPCO buys DC land for local Constellation office.
newsitem.headline: PEPCO buys DC land for local Constellation office.

text.p: Potomac Electric Power Co said Wednesday it had signed a contract to buy land in Washington, DC to build a $90 million regional headquarters for Constellation Energy Corp.

The announcement was made in a bid to stem local concerns that Constellation, the company that would be formed in PEPCO's pending merger with Baltimore Gas and Electric Co, would pull jobs out of the District of Columbia.
"By undertaking a project of this magnitude, Constellation Energy would continue PEPCO's 100-year commitment to the District," PEPCO president John Derrick said in a statement.
In hearings last month on the merger, DC Public Service Commissioners and consumer groups repeatedly raised concern about the merger's impact on PEPCO jobs in the district.

The company said Wednesday the land purchase, development, and construction would result in $4.5 million in one-time revenue to the District of Columbia, and $1.7 million in annual tax payments to the city.
If the merger is approved, the new building would house more than 1,300 Constellation Energy workers, PEPCO said.
The companies are awaiting approvals from Maryland, District of Columbia, and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
